info.title: Finero Public API
info.description:
Tenant-scoped public API for Finero — AR / cash-flow automation. Authenticate every request with `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` (keys are created in Settings → API and are tenant-owned). All data belongs to the key's tenant; no request input can address another tenant. Two permissions exist: **admin** keys can call every operation; **readonly** keys only operations without side effects (`x-permission: readonly`). Lists are cursor-paginated (limit 1–100, follow pagination.next_cursor). Request bodies are capped at 64 KiB. Rate limits: 120/min per key and 600/min per tenant, both fixed 60-second windows. EVERY response that reached the limiter carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until the window resets) and `RateLimit-Policy` (both quotas, static), plus the same figures as the newer combined `RateLimit` field. Pace against them rather than waiting to be refused. The triple describes whichever quota is CLOSEST TO REFUSING, so a key that is fine may still show little headroom when the tenant is busy. The counters are shared server-side, not per-instance, so the numbers are exact rather than approximate. Requests rejected BEFORE the limiter — unknown path, bad credentials, wrong method — consume no quota and carry no rate-limit fields. 429 adds `Retry-After` in seconds (RFC 9110); waiting that long is enough, and retrying sooner is refused again. Failed-authentication attempts are limited separately per source IP; that quota is deliberately not published. The windows are FIXED rather than sliding, so a burst spanning a boundary can pass up to twice the limit before being refused — do not treat the limit as a hard ceiling over less than two windows. `RateLimit-Remaining` RISES when a window rolls, for the same reason; an increase is the quota refilling, not an error. Watch `RateLimit-Reset` jump upward to tell a roll from a miscount. A 503 is not the limiter: under extreme concurrency the platform sheds load before the request reaches Finero, so it carries neither rate-limit fields nor Retry-After. Back off and retry. Decimal money amounts are exact strings (never floats); *_minor amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

**There is a second way in.** This API is for systems and unattended automation, authenticated by a tenant API key that acts as the WORKSPACE. If instead a person is present and connecting an AI assistant to their own workspace, use the Finero MCP server at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp` — Model Context Protocol over the Streamable HTTP transport (JSON-RPC 2.0, `MCP-Protocol-Version` 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26), authorized with OAuth 2.1 so the session acts as THAT PERSON. Its `server.json` manifest — the MCP registry's published format — is at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp/server.json`. It is read-mostly — 24 tools (list_tasks, dismiss_task, summarize_aging, list_customer_aging, list_aging_installments, list_invoices, summarize_invoices, get_invoice, list_payment_integrations, list_payments, list_workflows, list_workflow_executions, list_erp_connections, list_sync_runs, get_sync_run, start_erp_sync, list_payment_links, get_payment_link, create_payment_links, list_scheduled_emails, update_scheduled_email, delete_scheduled_email, push_payment_receipts, deactivate_payment_link). An agent may do what its person may: issue payment links (one, or a split of up to 12) and withdraw them, and reschedule or cancel their emails; an admin's agent may also start an ERP sync and release held receipts to the ERP. It can never send email it has written, or take or move money. Its OAuth scopes are declared in RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, which also names the authorization server. The two are not interchangeable: if you hold an API key, use this API.

get.description:
Current installment-level aging in the workspace timezone, read from the PAYMENT SCHEDULE rather than the invoice header. A row counts when the installment is live, still owes money, is not closed in the source, and has a due date; removed and retired records never count. The invoice's status is not consulted, so debt the ERP has locked is still counted; `collectible` on each row says whether Finero can act on it. Balances are the maintained ERP/Finero reconciled figures, aged by due date: today or future, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, or over 90 days. Absent by design: an installment with NO due date, which cannot be aged, and a CREDIT balance, which Finero never allocates against a debt. No historical reconstruction or FX. Totals cover all matching rows, per currency. Summary aggregates into `totals` and carries NEITHER `data` nor `pagination`: it is not a list. Customer and installment lists carry both. Use customer_key and bucket for drilldown. Cursors require unchanged query and report revision; restart on invalid_cursor. Invoice-summary due filters select whole invoices, not installment aging.

Available to **admin and readonly** API keys (no side effects).

get.description:
Lists the tenant's ERP connections (safe status metadata only — never credentials, hosts, or configuration). Connecting a new ERP and configuring what it syncs are managed inside the Finero app; starting a pull and changing the pull cadence can be done here.

Available to **admin and readonly** API keys (no side effects).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–100. Default 25.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's pagination.next_cursor.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Ordering is ALWAYS by when the record was CREATED in Finero, never by when it changed — `updated_since` narrows the set but does not reorder it, so the most recently updated row is not necessarily first. Creation time is immutable, which is what lets the cursor stay stable: ordering by a value that changes would move a row mid-walk and make a page skip or repeat it. Default desc (newest first by creation time).

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description: Return pagination.total_count — the number of rows matching the filters, ignoring paging. It is the SAME number on every page, including alongside a cursor. Off by default: an exact count scans the whole filtered set, so asking on each page pays repeatedly for an answer that does not change — ask on the first request and keep it.

id.description: ERP connection id — use as connection_id when starting a sync run.

provider.description: ERP system this connection syncs from.

pull_mode.description: How invoices are read from the ERP. `rest_api` reads the receivables REST resource with its payment schedules; `publisher_report` reads invoice headers from an Analytics Publisher report, so every invoice from that connection is collected as a whole — installments and contact names are never present. Both methods sync incrementally (changes since the last sync) and run a complete pass at least once a day, which is when an invoice that vanished from the ERP or from the report is marked no longer present. Read-only: the method is chosen when a workspace admin connects the ERP.

payment_push_transport.description: HOW a payment's receipt is pushed to the ERP. `rest` — the receivables REST resource. `soap` — the ERP's receipt SOAP services, offered only on a `publisher_report` connection, which then uses its report's SOAP user for everything and holds no OAuth client. Either way an accepted receipt reads `erp_push_status: posted`. Read-only: the transport is chosen when a workspace admin connects the ERP.

payment_push_mode.description: WHEN a payment collected through Finero is pushed to the ERP as a receipt. `auto` — right after the payment settles, without anyone acting. `manual` — the receipt is created at settlement but HELD until a workspace admin releases it, one or many at a time (POST /v1/payments/erp-push); a held payment reads `erp_push_status: held`. Releasing pushes each receipt on its own, so one failure never affects another. Switching from manual to auto releases everything held on the connection. Set with POST /v1/erp-connections/{connectionId}/payment-push-mode.

status.description: Connection health, and therefore whether the invoice data you are reading is CURRENT. `connected` means pulls are working. `requires_reauthentication` means the credential is missing, expired or revoked: scheduled pulls pause until a workspace admin reconnects it in the Finero app, so nothing new arrives and every figure is only as fresh as `last_successful_sync_at` - say so when you report numbers. `temporarily_unavailable` is the ERP being unreachable and usually clears itself. `disconnected` means the connection is switched off. In any state but `connected`, compare `last_successful_sync_at` against `last_sync_at`: a LATER `last_sync_at` means runs are still happening and not completing.

last_sync_at.description: When a sync run last finished, whatever its outcome. Use last_successful_sync_at to judge freshness (ISO 8601 UTC).

last_successful_sync_at.description: When a sync run last completed its walk of the ERP: a `success` run, or a `partial` one that only skipped invoices (its `error_summary` is null). Freshness of the imported data (ISO 8601 UTC).

auto_sync_enabled.description: Whether scheduled auto-sync is on. False is the workspace's "off" choice - manual pulls still work, and `auto_sync_interval_minutes` keeps the cadence that applies when it is turned back on. True still requires connected health and a stored credential; reconnection restores the retained schedule after a missing-credential failure.

auto_sync_interval_minutes.description: How often Finero pulls this connection automatically, in minutes. A workspace admin chooses it: 10 to 1440 (24 hours). Read it together with `auto_sync_enabled` - when that is false there is no automatic pull at all and this value is simply the setting kept for when it is turned back on. It is a FLOOR rather than an appointment: a connection is pulled on the first scheduled check after this much time has passed, typically within a minute of it.

pull_invoice_date_from.description: Oldest invoice date this connection imports, inclusive. null means no limit. This is why an invoice that exists in the ERP may be absent here: it is dated before the limit. Changing it never deletes invoices already imported (YYYY-MM-DD).

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page — pass as ?cursor=. Null when there are no further results.

get.description:
Lists the tenant's synced invoices, newest first by creation time. Cursor-paginated: pass `limit` (1–100) and send pagination.next_cursor back as `cursor` until has_more is false. To learn HOW MANY rows match without walking every page, pass `include_total=true` once and read pagination.total_count. Filters are allowlisted; combine freely. collection_status filters like any other field — it is a stored, indexed value, so it pages and counts exactly as the rest do and combines with ?include_total=true.

Available to **admin and readonly** API keys (no side effects).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1–100. Default 25.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's pagination.next_cursor.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Ordering is ALWAYS by when the record was CREATED in Finero, never by when it changed — `updated_since` narrows the set but does not reorder it, so the most recently updated row is not necessarily first. Creation time is immutable, which is what lets the cursor stay stable: ordering by a value that changes would move a row mid-walk and make a page skip or repeat it. Default desc (newest first by creation time).

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description: Return pagination.total_count — the number of rows matching the filters, ignoring paging. It is the SAME number on every page, including alongside a cursor. Off by default: an exact count scans the whole filtered set, so asking on each page pays repeatedly for an answer that does not change — ask on the first request and keep it.

parameters.name: collection_status
parameters.description: Return only invoices with this collection status — Finero's own payment record, so paid means FINERO collected it and an invoice settled elsewhere is inactive. Combines with every other filter, and with include_total.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Filter by ISO 4217 currency code.

parameters.name: invoice_number
parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the ERP invoice number.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: Filter by ERP connection.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Only invoices updated at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. `updated_at` moves when the invoice's own data changes (an ERP delivery, a retirement, an edit), NOT when only Finero's collection state does (`collection_status`, `collection_outstanding`, `amount_collected`, `erp_push_state`, `has_active_payment_link`): poll `GET /v1/payments?confirmed_since=` for collections. The bound INCLUDES its own timestamp, so polling with the newest `updated_at` you have seen returns that row again every time - expected, and not a change.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: Only invoices for this customer, by the stable `customer.id` on the invoice. This is the ONLY safe way to total one customer's exposure — grouping by name merges two customers who share one, and grouping by email splits a customer across its billing addresses.

parameters.name: erp_push_state
parameters.description: Only invoices whose payment write-back to the ERP is in this state. `failed` is the one to watch: money Finero collected is not represented in the ERP, so its own balance overstates what is owed — and without this filter a stuck invoice is invisible unless you already know its number.

parameters.name: has_active_payment_link
parameters.description: Only invoices with (`true`) or without (`false`) an active Finero payment link. Combine `false` with `collection_status=open` and `due_before` for the overdue-and-unlinked worklist in one call.

parameters.name: due_before
parameters.description: Only invoices whose collection_due_date is on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD), INCLUSIVE. The overdue worklist is due_before=<today> with collection_status=open. FILTERS ON collection_due_date, so an invoice that has none is excluded — and one has none precisely when nothing on it is collectible, which is also when it can still owe money. Date bands therefore never sum to the whole book: check a total against a call with no date filter, never against the bands. `amount_collected` under ANY date filter is PARTIAL and never a collected total: a fully paid invoice has no `collection_due_date` so its collections drop out, while a partly collected OPEN invoice keeps its own and stays in. Ask with no date filter for what was collected.

parameters.name: due_after
parameters.description: Only invoices whose collection_due_date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD), INCLUSIVE. Combine with due_before for one aging bucket — but because BOTH ends include their own date, adjacent bands must not share a boundary: use due_before=X then due_after=<X plus one day>, or every invoice dated exactly X is counted twice and the profile sums to more than the book. Every `collection_due_date` exclusion and the partial-`amount_collected` caveat described on `due_before` applies here identically.

collection_mode.description: Collect from the invoice header or its real installment schedule.

currency.description: Invoice currency. ISO 4217 alphabetic code, e.g. "USD".

total_amount.description: Invoice total. Null while the ERP has none yet (a draft). Exact decimal string at the CURRENCY'S own scale — USD "1250.00", JPY "1250", BHD "1250.000". Never parse as float for arithmetic.

Null if nothing is collectible or no due date is available. Use Aging operations for the full dated balance report. Filter with due_before / due_after.

last_synced_at.description: When Finero last read this invoice FROM the ERP. Use it to ask whether a row is still current with your ERP — `updated_at` cannot answer that, because Finero's own writes to the invoice move it too (marking an invoice no longer present; recording a payment on an invoice created in Finero), so a row can look freshly updated while the ERP has not been heard from in weeks. Finero's collection state alone does not move `updated_at`. Null for invoices created in Finero, which have no ERP to read from, and for a few rows that predate the field. (ISO 8601 UTC).

collection_outstanding.description: What Finero still has to collect on this invoice, as an exact decimal string. Null while the ERP has no amount yet (a draft): unknown, never zero. THIS IS THE FIELD THAT ACCOUNTS FOR PAYMENTS FINERO HAS ALREADY TAKEN, including before your ERP has been told about them; payments and changes made in your ERP arrive with the next sync. Zero for an invoice no longer present in your ERP. Sum this for what is owed: the summary's totals are this sum.

amount_collected.description: How much Finero has confirmed collected on this invoice, as an exact decimal string. Money taken through a Finero payment link only - a payment made directly to you, or settled in your ERP, is not counted here and leaves this at zero.

erp_push_state.description: How far the money Finero collected has got into your ERP, or null when Finero has collected nothing on this invoice. `held` means the connection pushes receipts manually and an admin has not released this one yet; `pending` means the push is queued and `processing` that it is in flight - under all three, the ERP has not been told yet. `posted` means the ERP accepted the receipt - Finero's part ends there, and what the ERP does with it afterwards (allocating it, or reversing it) is the ERP's business. `failed` means the receipt never reached the ERP, so your ERP still shows that money as owed until someone acts. Finero retries a `failed` push every 15 minutes for 24 hours when the ERP was simply unreachable; any other cause waits for a person, because retrying cannot fix it. The WORST state across the invoice's pushes is reported, because this field exists to surface a problem and a majority would hide one. NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH a payment's `erp_push_status`: that one is a SINGLE payment's own push, while this rolls up every push on the invoice.

collection_status.description: ANSWER "HAS THIS INVOICE BEEN PAID?" FROM THIS FIELD. `paid` MEANS THE INVOICE IS PAID - nothing is left to collect on it - and it is the most current answer available: Finero knows the moment it collects, and your ERP finds out afterwards. `paid` REQUIRES TWO THINGS: Finero collected on it, AND no collection target has a balance outstanding. An invoice where Finero collected part and the remainder is excluded or otherwise blocked reads `inactive`, not `paid` — so `paid` can never hide money that is still owed. `open` means the invoice or a real installment is COLLECTIBLE by Finero — that, and nothing more. Whether a payment link or reminder actually goes out is a SEPARATE question, decided by which workflows this workspace has switched on, and no status on this invoice answers it. `inactive` is everything else. THE CONVERSE DOES NOT HOLD, and this is the one trap: NOT-`paid` does not mean unpaid. An invoice the customer settled directly with you, outside Finero, reads `inactive` - Finero did not take that money, so it cannot report having collected it. `paid` is conclusive; anything else means find out why. `paid` ALSO DOES NOT SAY HOW MUCH FINERO COLLECTED: an invoice settled by mixed paths - one installment direct to you, the rest through Finero - is still `paid`. Compare `amount_collected` against `total_amount` to attribute it. YOUR ERP LAGS THIS FIELD: it may still show a balance on a `paid` invoice until it applies Finero's receipt - NOT a reason to doubt the status. Read `erp_push_state` to tell ordinary lag from a push that will stay unreflected until someone acts. An invoice finalised with a balance still reads `inactive` when nothing on it can be collected - every installment excluded from collections, closed in your ERP, or the invoice has no billing email or a currency no connected payment provider can charge - and THE MONEY IS NOT WRITTEN OFF: `collection_outstanding` still carries it. Sum `collection_outstanding` for what is OWED - but it is populated on invoices nothing can be collected from, so filter to `collection_status=open` for what can actually be collected, and read each installment's `collectible` to see which parts. Invoice status blocks collection only when enabled on the connection; re-enabling requires fresh status. Other safeguards still apply. Inactive may also mean no balance outstanding, the ERP no longer has the invoice, or no payment schedule in installment mode. Invoice-only mode needs no schedule. A removed invoice can resume collection if a later sync finds it.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: Invoice id.

collection_mode.description: Collect from the invoice header or its real installment schedule.

block_reasons.description: INVOICE MODE ONLY (`collection_mode: invoice`), where the invoice itself is what Finero collects and there are no installments to carry this: WHY it is not collectible, as stable codes — empty when nothing blocks it. The same codes, and the same derivation, as an installment's `block_reasons`; in installment mode read them there instead. Meanings: https://app.getfinero.com/guide.

invoice_number.description: Human-readable local or ERP invoice number.

currency.description: Invoice currency. ISO 4217 alphabetic code, e.g. "USD".

total_amount.description: Invoice total. Null while the ERP has none yet (a draft). Exact decimal string at the CURRENCY'S own scale — USD "1250.00", JPY "1250", BHD "1250.000". Never parse as float for arithmetic.

payment_terms.description: The invoice's payment terms exactly as your ERP names them (for example `NET30`). Informational: due dates come from `due_date` and `collection_due_date`, never from the terms. Null when the ERP sent none, when the connection does not collect them, and for local invoices.

collection_due_date.description: Due date for collectible invoice worklists: the invoice header date in invoice mode, or the earliest collectible installment date in installment mode. Null if nothing is collectible or no due date is available. Use Aging operations for the full dated balance report. Filter with due_before / due_after.

last_synced_at.description: When Finero last read this invoice FROM the ERP. Use it to ask whether a row is still current with your ERP — `updated_at` cannot answer that, because Finero's own writes to the invoice move it too (marking an invoice no longer present; recording a payment on an invoice created in Finero), so a row can look freshly updated while the ERP has not been heard from in weeks. Finero's collection state alone does not move `updated_at`. Null for invoices created in Finero, which have no ERP to read from, and for a few rows that predate the field. (ISO 8601 UTC).

collection_outstanding.description: What Finero still has to collect on this invoice, as an exact decimal string. Null while the ERP has no amount yet (a draft): unknown, never zero. THIS IS THE FIELD THAT ACCOUNTS FOR PAYMENTS FINERO HAS ALREADY TAKEN, including before your ERP has been told about them; payments and changes made in your ERP arrive with the next sync. Zero for an invoice no longer present in your ERP. Sum this for what is owed: the summary's totals are this sum.

amount_collected.description: How much Finero has confirmed collected on this invoice, as an exact decimal string. Money taken through a Finero payment link only - a payment made directly to you, or settled in your ERP, is not counted here and leaves this at zero.

erp_push_state.description: How far the money Finero collected has got into your ERP, or null when Finero has collected nothing on this invoice. `held` means the connection pushes receipts manually and an admin has not released this one yet; `pending` means the push is queued and `processing` that it is in flight - under all three, the ERP has not been told yet. `posted` means the ERP accepted the receipt - Finero's part ends there, and what the ERP does with it afterwards (allocating it, or reversing it) is the ERP's business. `failed` means the receipt never reached the ERP, so your ERP still shows that money as owed until someone acts. Finero retries a `failed` push every 15 minutes for 24 hours when the ERP was simply unreachable; any other cause waits for a person, because retrying cannot fix it. The WORST state across the invoice's pushes is reported, because this field exists to surface a problem and a majority would hide one. NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH a payment's `erp_push_status`: that one is a SINGLE payment's own push, while this rolls up every push on the invoice.

collection_status.description: ANSWER "HAS THIS INVOICE BEEN PAID?" FROM THIS FIELD. `paid` MEANS THE INVOICE IS PAID - nothing is left to collect on it - and it is the most current answer available: Finero knows the moment it collects, and your ERP finds out afterwards. `paid` REQUIRES TWO THINGS: Finero collected on it, AND no collection target has a balance outstanding. An invoice where Finero collected part and the remainder is excluded or otherwise blocked reads `inactive`, not `paid` — so `paid` can never hide money that is still owed. `open` means the invoice or a real installment is COLLECTIBLE by Finero — that, and nothing more. Whether a payment link or reminder actually goes out is a SEPARATE question, decided by which workflows this workspace has switched on, and no status on this invoice answers it. `inactive` is everything else. THE CONVERSE DOES NOT HOLD, and this is the one trap: NOT-`paid` does not mean unpaid. An invoice the customer settled directly with you, outside Finero, reads `inactive` - Finero did not take that money, so it cannot report having collected it. `paid` is conclusive; anything else means find out why. `paid` ALSO DOES NOT SAY HOW MUCH FINERO COLLECTED: an invoice settled by mixed paths - one installment direct to you, the rest through Finero - is still `paid`. Compare `amount_collected` against `total_amount` to attribute it. YOUR ERP LAGS THIS FIELD: it may still show a balance on a `paid` invoice until it applies Finero's receipt - NOT a reason to doubt the status. Read `erp_push_state` to tell ordinary lag from a push that will stay unreflected until someone acts. An invoice finalised with a balance still reads `inactive` when nothing on it can be collected - every installment excluded from collections, closed in your ERP, or the invoice has no billing email or a currency no connected payment provider can charge - and THE MONEY IS NOT WRITTEN OFF: `collection_outstanding` still carries it. Sum `collection_outstanding` for what is OWED - but it is populated on invoices nothing can be collected from, so filter to `collection_status=open` for what can actually be collected, and read each installment's `collectible` to see which parts. Invoice status blocks collection only when enabled on the connection; re-enabling requires fresh status. Other safeguards still apply. Inactive may also mean no balance outstanding, the ERP no longer has the invoice, or no payment schedule in installment mode. Invoice-only mode needs no schedule. A removed invoice can resume collection if a later sync finds it.

has_active_payment_link.description: Whether a Finero payment link is currently active on any installment of this invoice. `false` on an open invoice is the worklist: something is owed and nothing has been sent to collect it. Filter on it rather than joining against the payment-link list.

customer.description: Bill-to customer details embedded on the invoice. There is no customer ENDPOINT, but there is a stable customer KEY — see `id`.

id.description: STABLE CUSTOMER KEY — group by this, never by name or email. number.description: The business account number from the linked customer; id is Finero's generated UUID. Null when the invoice has no resolved account.

contact_name.description: The person named on the invoice as the bill-to contact. Display only: it is never used to identify anyone and nothing in Finero branches on it, because an ERP can carry two people with the same name on one account. Null when the ERP sends none, or when the workspace has switched the Contact name pull field off for this connector. For a sole trader it may equal name.

email.description: Billing email the payment-link email is sent to.

origin.description: Provenance / system of record: local = the invoice exists only in Finero; erp = an ERP connection owns (or will own) the record.

connection_id.description: The exact ERP connection associated with this invoice.

installments.description: The invoice's installments, ordered by sequence.

id.description: Installment id — use as installment_id when creating a payment link.

original_amount.description: Original installment amount. Exact decimal string at the CURRENCY'S own scale — USD "1250.00", JPY "1250", BHD "1250.000". Never parse as float for arithmetic.

collection_status.description: What Finero is doing about collecting THIS installment. Same three values as the invoice's `collection_status`, and it inherits that verdict: an installment of an `inactive` invoice is `inactive`. `paid` MEANS THIS INSTALLMENT IS PAID - nothing is left on it - and it is the current answer even while your ERP still shows a balance, which lags. The converse does not hold: an installment settled directly in your ERP reads `inactive`, because Finero did not take that money, so NOT-`paid` is not the same as unpaid. `open` requires THREE things together: an outstanding balance, `collectible` being true, and the ERP's own status saying the installment is still open - each connector declares which of its status values mean that. Where there is no provider status to judge (an invoice created in Finero) the first two decide alone. IT REPORTS WHAT FINERO IS DOING, NOT WHAT IS OWED: an installment that is genuinely outstanding but blocked - excluded, no billing email, a currency no connected provider can charge - reads `inactive`, because Finero is not collecting it. get.summary: Count invoices by collection status, and total the money
get.description:
Answers 'how many, and how much' in ONE request. Returns counts per collection_status, outstanding and collected money per currency, and the customers owed the most (`by_customer`, capped by `customer_limit`), over the filters listInvoices accepts (all but `invoice_number`). Use this instead of paging every invoice and adding it up: collection_status is derived from Finero's own payment record and is not something a caller can compute from the fields it receives, and money must never be summed or ranked across currencies, so `by_customer` ranks within each. Exact at any workspace size: the counts come from an indexed column, so nothing is capped and nothing is sampled. Every filter listInvoices accepts except `invoice_number` works here too — pair `due_after` with `due_before` to select whole invoices by their earliest collectible due date. For installment-level aging use the Aging operations; an invoice can span multiple aging buckets.

Available to **admin and readonly** API keys (no side effects).

parameters.name: collection_status
parameters.description: Count and total only invoices with this collection status. NOT derivable from the unfiltered response: `by_collection_status` already gives the counts, but `by_currency` aggregates money across every status — so 'how much is still open, per currency' needs this filter. An `inactive` invoice can carry a real balance it will never collect, and summing across statuses buries that in the same number.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Filter by ISO 4217 currency code.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: Filter by ERP connection.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Only invoices updated at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. `updated_at` moves when the invoice's own data changes (an ERP delivery, a retirement, an edit), NOT when only Finero's collection state does (`collection_status`, `collection_outstanding`, `amount_collected`, `erp_push_state`, `has_active_payment_link`): poll `GET /v1/payments?confirmed_since=` for collections. The bound INCLUDES its own timestamp, so polling with the newest `updated_at` you have seen returns that row again every time - expected, and not a change.

parameters.name: customer_id
parameters.description: Only count invoices for this customer, by the stable `customer.id`. One call gives that customer's whole exposure, per currency — the safe alternative to paging the book and grouping by name.

parameters.name: erp_push_state
parameters.description: Only count invoices whose payment write-back to the ERP is in this state. `erp_push_state=failed` answers 'how much money has Finero collected that the ERP does not know about?' in one call.

parameters.name: has_active_payment_link
parameters.description: Only count invoices with (`true`) or without (`false`) an active Finero payment link — the same filter the list accepts, so the money behind an unlinked worklist is one call.

parameters.name: due_before
parameters.description: Only invoices whose collection_due_date is on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD), INCLUSIVE. The overdue worklist is due_before=<today> with collection_status=open. FILTERS ON collection_due_date, so an invoice that has none is excluded — and one has none precisely when nothing on it is collectible, which is also when it can still owe money. Date bands therefore never sum to the whole book: check a total against a call with no date filter, never against the bands. `amount_collected` under ANY date filter is PARTIAL and never a collected total: a fully paid invoice has no `collection_due_date` so its collections drop out, while a partly collected OPEN invoice keeps its own and stays in. Ask with no date filter for what was collected.

parameters.name: due_after
parameters.description: Only invoices whose collection_due_date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD), INCLUSIVE. Combine with due_before for one aging bucket — but because BOTH ends include their own date, adjacent bands must not share a boundary: use due_before=X then due_after=<X plus one day>, or every invoice dated exactly X is counted twice and the profile sums to more than the book. Every `collection_due_date` exclusion and the partial-`amount_collected` caveat described on `due_before` applies here identically.

parameters.name: customer_limit
parameters.description: How many `by_customer` rows to return (default 25, max 100), drawn evenly across currencies so a short list never omits one. Read `by_customer_total` to know whether the cap hid rows.

total.description: Invoices matching the filters. An exact count, never an estimate — and the number to trust for 'how many are there'.

by_collection_status.description: Count per collection status, over every invoice matching the filters. The three are exhaustive and sum to `total`. `paid` counts invoices with nothing left to collect that Finero collected on — including one settled by MIXED paths, part in your ERP and part through Finero. The full rule is on the invoice's own `collection_status`; it is not restated here so the two cannot disagree.

paid.description: Invoices with nothing left to collect that Finero collected on. See `collection_status` on the invoice for the full rule.

open.description: Invoices with an invoice-level or installment balance Finero can collect. See `collection_status` on the invoice for the full rule.

inactive.description: Invoices Finero is not collecting and did not collect — settled entirely outside Finero, cancelled, or with nothing collectible left. NOT the same as paid, and NOT the same as unpaid.

inactive_nothing_to_collect.description: The subset of `inactive` with nothing left to collect — settled outside Finero, cancelled, a draft, empty, a credit, or no longer present in your ERP. `inactive` minus this is the count with money STUCK on it: owed, and not collectible right now. This is Finero's own answer (its `collection_outstanding` at or below zero), not the ERP's balance, so it stays correct while the ERP lags.

by_currency.description: Money per ISO 4217 currency, over every invoice matching the filters. NEVER summed across currencies — a single total over a mixed-currency workspace is a wrong number, not a shorter one. An invoice no longer present in your ERP owes nothing here (money already collected on it still counts), as in Aging.

currency.description: Uppercased. NULL when the connector supplied no currency: that money is still owed and still counted, but nothing can be collected against it until the ERP supplies a code. Never merge that bucket into another. ISO 4217 alphabetic code, e.g. "USD".

collection_outstanding.description: What is still outstanding after Finero's own collections, in this currency. Exact decimal string at that currency's own scale — USD reads 2989.00, JPY 1560817, BHD 2.010. CAUTION: this is what is OWED, not what is collectible — it includes invoices Finero is blocked from collecting (see an installment's block_reasons). Filtering to collection_status=open is the right total of what Finero can act on. It can still include an OPEN invoice's blocked installment — when one specific invoice matters, its detail says per installment what is collectible; that is a per-invoice check, never a workspace walk.

amount_collected.description: What Finero has collected, in this currency. Exact decimal string at that currency's scale. IT INCLUDES TEST-MODE MONEY, exactly as the invoice's own field does, so the two cannot disagree — but test money is NOT revenue. Real cash is this figure MINUS `amount_collected_test_mode` beside it; when they are equal, nothing real has been collected and reporting this as income would be wrong.

amount_collected_test_mode.description: How much of `amount_collected` came from TEST-mode payments, in this currency. Exact decimal string at that currency's scale. Subtract for real cash. The only aggregate that separates the two — `list_payments` has `mode` per payment, but paging it is what this call avoids.

by_customer.description: WHO OWES THE MOST: the customers with money outstanding, over the same filters as everything else here. One row per (customer, currency) — a customer billed in two currencies is two rows, because money is never summed across currencies and, for the same reason, never ranked across them: `collection_outstanding` ranks WITHIN a currency, grouped by currency and largest first inside each. Narrow with `currency` to rank one book. Capped by `customer_limit` (default 25, max 100), drawn evenly across currencies so a short list never omits one; `by_customer_total` says how many rows exist, so a capped answer never reads as complete. This is the aggregate that replaces paging every invoice and grouping by `customer.id` client-side — there is deliberately no customer endpoint.

customer_id.description: The stable `customer.id` carried on each invoice. NULL for invoices the connector attached to no customer: that money is still owed and is one honest row, not dropped.

customer_name.description: The customer's display name as the ERP supplied it; null when it supplied none.

currency.description: Uppercased; NULL when the connector supplied no currency. ISO 4217 alphabetic code, e.g. "USD".

collection_outstanding.description: What this customer still owes in this currency after Finero's collections, as an exact decimal string at that currency's scale — the same figure and format as `by_currency`, so the rows for one currency sum to that bucket.

amount_collected.description: What Finero has collected from this customer in this currency, as an exact decimal string at that currency's scale. TEST-MODE MONEY IS INCLUDED, as on the invoice, and is not split out per customer: before reporting it as revenue, check the currency's `amount_collected_test_mode` in `by_currency` (or `mode` per payment in list_payments).

invoice_count.description: How many of this customer's invoices in this currency carry money (outstanding or collected). An invoice collected in full still counts here — the aging report's `invoice_count` counts only what is still owed, so it can be lower for the same customer.

by_customer_total.description: How many (customer, currency) rows matched in total. When it exceeds the length of `by_customer`, the list was capped by `customer_limit` — raise it, or narrow the filters.

A task is work Finero asks a person to do on an invoice; today the one type is payment_arrangement: the Payment Arrangement workflow matched the invoice, so a person sets up its payment links. Filter state=open for the invoices still waiting for their first payment link; each row names its invoice (`invoice_number`). Cursor-paginated: pass `limit` (1–100) and send pagination.next_cursor back as `cursor` until has_more is false. To learn HOW MANY rows match without walking every page, pass `include_total=true` once and read pagination.total_count.

Available to **admin and readonly** API keys (no side effects).

parameters.description: Page size, 1–100. Default 25.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's pagination.next_cursor.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Ordering is ALWAYS by when the record was CREATED in Finero, never by when it changed — `updated_since` narrows the set but does not reorder it, so the most recently updated row is not necessarily first. Creation time is immutable, which is what lets the cursor stay stable: ordering by a value that changes would move a row mid-walk and make a page skip or repeat it. Default desc (newest first by creation time).

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description: Return pagination.total_count — the number of rows matching the filters, ignoring paging. It is the SAME number on every page, including alongside a cursor. Off by default: an exact count scans the whole filtered set, so asking on each page pays repeatedly for an answer that does not change — ask on the first request and keep it.

get.description:
Every workflow Finero has, what each one does, what causes it to run, and which are switched on for this workspace — plus what every execution reason code means. For payment-link emails it also reports whether new links send immediately or before their link-owned due date, including the tenant-local send time. Read this to understand how the automations relate to each other: creating a payment link is what sends the customer the payment email, so the same email goes out whether the link was created by the automation, by hand in Finero, or through this API. The set is closed and small, so this operation is not paginated.

Available to **admin and readonly** API keys (no side effects).

workflows.description: Every workflow Finero has, with this workspace's switches merged in.

audience.description: Who this workflow contacts directly. `none` means it contacts nobody — its effects reach people only through the workflows it fires.

enabled.description: Whether the workflow is on for this workspace.

configured.description: Whether anyone has ever set this workflow up. False with `enabled` false means never set up, which is a different answer from deliberately switched off.

never_does.description: Limits worth stating, because they are what people assume wrongly.

triggers.description: Its triggers, and whether each is on here.

key.description: The switch an administrator toggles, or null when the workflow has no per-trigger switch and its own on/off is the switch.

title.description: How the switch reads in Finero.

enabled.description: Whether this trigger is on for this workspace.

fired_by.description: What causes this trigger to fire — including things a person does, not only automated ones.

effect.description: What actually happens when it fires.

delivery_timing.description: Configured timing for this trigger, or null when the trigger has no timing control.

mode.description: When a new payment-link email is planned.

days_before.description: Calendar days before the link-owned payment due date, or null.

local_time.description: Tenant-local 24-hour HH:mm send time, or null for immediate delivery. Defaults to 09:00 when older settings omit it.

timezone_source.description: The timezone is inherited from the tenant; clients never supply it.

past_due_behavior.description: What happens when the calculated instant has already passed.

causes.description: Workflows this one fires. This is the relationship between automations: creating a payment link is what sends the customer the email.

automatic.description: What Finero does on its own, without being asked.

timing.description: When it runs, and how late a missed one can be.

history.description: Where the record of what it did lives, and whether this API exposes it. Read this before concluding from an empty execution list that nothing happened.

updated_at.description: When the configuration was last changed (ISO 8601 UTC).

block_reasons.description: Every code an installment's `block_reasons` can carry, and what each means. A DIFFERENT vocabulary from `reason_codes` below: these say why one installment cannot be collected, those say why an automation run did not do something.

code.description: The value that appears in an installment's `block_reasons`.

label.description: How it reads on screen in Finero.

meaning.description: What it means, and the next move.

reason_codes.description: Every reason code an execution can carry, and what each means. Flat, because a code is not owned by one workflow.

code.description: The value that appears as an execution's `reason_code`.

meaning.description: What it means, in plain words.

fault.description: Where the problem is: `configuration` a Finero setting, `data` the ERP data, `provider` the payment or email provider, `finero` a Finero fault, `none` not a fault at all.

resolution.description: What to do about it, and by whom.

workflows.name: Payment Link Automation
workflows.does: Gives each NEW invoice — one that reaches Finero while this workflow is on — one try once it is ready for collection (a draft waits until your ERP completes it): a hosted payment link for every installment Finero can collect on, through the workspace's connected payment processor. Invoices already in Finero when it is switched on are never touched, and an invoice is never tried twice. It contacts nobody itself — the customer learns about the link only if the Email Notification workflow is on.
never_does: Send anything to a customer. Creating the link and emailing it are two workflows.
Charge a card or move money. The customer pays through the link when they choose to.
Write anything back to your ERP.
Create a second link for an installment that already has a live one.
Look at an invoice again after its one try — a link that fails, or is later withdrawn or closed, is replaced by a person.
Touch invoices that were already in Finero when it was switched on.
Decide which invoices are collectible — that follows from your ERP data.

triggers.title: When a new invoice reaches Finero
fired_by: an ERP sync bringing in an invoice Finero did not have — tried right away by a sync someone starts by hand, otherwise within 15 minutes
an invoice being created in Finero
triggers.effect: One payment link per collectible installment, created through the connected processor.

causes.when: Always, when that trigger is on. Creating the link is what sends the email — so the SAME email goes out for a link created by hand in Finero or through the public API. It is a consequence of the link existing, not a step this automation performs.

operator_controls: Switch the whole workflow on or off. Switch it on after your first ERP sync: every invoice a sync brings in while it is on counts as new.
Which payment processor it uses — whichever one is connected.
automatic: Live payment links can never add up to more than an installment owes, enforced by the database, so a duplicate cannot be created even if two runs overlap.
Each new invoice is tried once, whatever the outcome; the outcome is in its history. A try cut short by an outage is not repeated.
A new invoice that is not ready yet waits, and gets its try once a later sync shows it ready; one that never becomes ready (paid or cancelled first) is never tried.
An invoice held by an open payment-arrangement task waits for the task to be dismissed, then gets its try.
One invoice failing never stops the rest of the batch.
workflows.timing: Immediately after a sync someone starts by hand, and otherwise within 15 minutes of the invoice arriving.
workflows.history: Every try is recorded — succeeded, skipped and failed, each with a reason code — and is readable through the workflow-executions endpoint, which keeps the latest 500 per workspace (a few more for a moment when tries are written at once).

workflows.name: Payment Arrangement
workflows.does: Opens a task when an invoice newly matches a configured ERP field rule: notifies an assigned workspace member, and keeps Auto Generate off that invoice until the task is dismissed.
never_does: Does not notify existing matches when enabled.
Does not create or replace links without a person's instruction.
Does not withdraw a task when the invoice later stops matching or the workflow is turned off.

triggers.title: Invoice starts matching
fired_by: A committed ERP sync changes a known nonmatch to a match, or imports a new matching invoice after activation.
triggers.effect: Opens one task for the invoice (one ever) and sends one notice on each configured channel. An invoice that already has a payment link gets a task that is already configured, and no notice.

operator_controls: Choose the ERP connection, invoice field, equals value, one workspace member and email, Slack or both.
automatic: Repeated syncs do not duplicate tasks or notices.
The invoice's first payment link, however it is created, configures the task.
Notices stop while the workflow is off.
workflows.timing: The task commits with the ERP change; the notice is sent within seconds and retried per channel.
workflows.history: The task records when it was configured or dismissed; it writes no workflow execution rows.

workflows.name: Email Notification
workflows.does: Emails the customer at the bill-to address on the invoice. Two triggers, switched on and off independently.
never_does: Email anyone other than the address on the invoice. The recipient is never chosen by a caller.
Send the same notification twice for one payment link — the database refuses a second one.
Run on its own. It only ever reacts to something else happening.

triggers.title: After a payment link is created
fired_by: Payment Link Automation creating a link
someone creating a payment link by hand in Finero
a payment link created through the public API
triggers.effect: The customer is emailed the link so they can pay online.

triggers.title: After an invoice is paid
fired_by: a payment being confirmed by the payment processor — every path that can confirm one fires this, so the email does not depend on any single one of them working
triggers.effect: The customer is emailed confirmation that their payment was received.

operator_controls: Switch each trigger on or off independently.
Send new payment-link emails immediately or a chosen number of days before the link-owned due date at a tenant-local time.
Choose the sending mailbox by connecting a Google mailbox; with none connected, Finero sends.
automatic: At most one email per trigger, payment link and recipient — enforced by the database, which is what makes it safe for several settlement paths to overlap as safety nets.
A notification that was never attempted — because a read failed, say — is picked up by a recovery sweep within about 15 minutes.
The amount in the email is the amount that link collects, never the invoice total.
workflows.timing: Payment-link emails send immediately by default, or at the configured time in the workspace timezone a chosen number of days before the link-owned due date. The default time is 09:00, and a calculated time in the past sends immediately. Payment confirmations send as soon as payment is confirmed.
workflows.history: Email attempts are recorded in Finero's notification history, which this API does not expose. NO workflow-execution row is written for an email — so an absent execution never means an email was not sent.

workflows.name: Internal Notification
workflows.does: Emails the workspace's own team at a configured address. Never reaches a customer.
never_does: Email a customer. The recipient is a setting, not the invoice's address.
Stop working when a connected Google mailbox does. It is always sent from Finero, deliberately, so alerts still arrive on the day that mailbox is disconnected or rate limited.

triggers.title: After an invoice is paid
fired_by: a payment being confirmed by the payment processor — the same moment that fires the customer-facing confirmation, and independent of it
triggers.effect: The team is emailed that a payment was confirmed. Sent whether or not the payment has reached the ERP yet.

operator_controls: Set the address your team is notified at. The address itself is not readable through this API.
automatic: Sent from Finero always, even with a Google mailbox connected.
Recovered by its own sweep within about 15 minutes if it was never attempted.
workflows.timing: Sent when a payment is confirmed. A missed one is recovered within about 15 minutes.
workflows.history: Recorded in Finero's notification history, which this API does not expose. No workflow-execution row is written.

reason_codes.meaning: Auto Generate skips this invoice: it has a payment-arrangement task, so a person sets up its payment links.
reason_codes.resolution: Create the payment links in Finero or with your connected AI assistant, or dismiss the task to give the invoice its Auto Generate try.

reason_codes.meaning: The workflow is switched off for this workspace, so nothing was attempted.
reason_codes.resolution: A workspace administrator switches it on in Finero, under Workflows.

reason_codes.meaning: The invoice is not marked ready to collect. Readiness comes from your ERP data, not from a Finero setting.
reason_codes.resolution: The invoice had its one automatic try. Once the ERP shows a collectible balance, create its payment link in Finero.

reason_codes.meaning: The invoice is ready, but not one installment on it can be charged — each is already paid, excluded from collections, or has nothing outstanding.
reason_codes.resolution: Read the installment's own block reason on the invoice. After correcting the ERP, create the payment link in Finero.

reason_codes.meaning: No payment processor is connected, so there is nothing to create a link with.
reason_codes.resolution: An administrator connects a payment processor in Finero, then creates the invoice's payment link; the automation tries each invoice once.

reason_codes.meaning: A payment processor is connected but Finero could not use it — the credential was rejected, or the processor could not be reached.
reason_codes.resolution: If the credential was rejected, an administrator reconnects the processor. Then create the invoice's payment link in Finero; the automation tries each invoice once.

reason_codes.meaning: The invoice or installment carries an amount Finero cannot read as money, or a balance below the smallest amount the payment processor can charge.
reason_codes.resolution: Correct the amount in the ERP, then create the payment link in Finero.

reason_codes.meaning: A live payment link already exists for that installment, so a second was not created.
reason_codes.resolution: Nothing is wrong — this is the duplicate protection working. The existing link is the one to use.

reason_codes.meaning: The amount owed changed after the link was created, so the old link no longer matches the invoice.
reason_codes.resolution: Nothing to do. Finero revalidates before a customer pays, so a stale amount is never charged.

reason_codes.meaning: The invoice is now billed in a different currency than the one the payment link was created in, so that link no longer matches the invoice.
reason_codes.resolution: Nothing to do. Finero revalidates before a customer pays, so the wrong currency is never charged.

reason_codes.meaning: The connected payment processor cannot charge the invoice's currency.
reason_codes.resolution: Connect a processor that supports that currency and create the link in Finero, or collect those invoices outside Finero.

reason_codes.meaning: The workspace's plan does not include payment links.
reason_codes.resolution: Change the plan. This is not a fault — retrying will keep producing the same answer.

reason_codes.meaning: The installment cannot be collected on: nothing is outstanding, it is excluded, or a payment landed while the link was being created.
reason_codes.resolution: Usually nothing — an already-collected installment is the ordinary case. Otherwise the block reason on the installment says which.

reason_codes.meaning: The payment processor failed in a way that is worth retrying.
reason_codes.resolution: Create the payment link in Finero once the processor is reachable; the automation tries each invoice once.

reason_codes.meaning: Finero contacted the email provider and could not learn whether the message went out. Belongs to the email path, not to automation runs.
reason_codes.resolution: It is deliberately not retried automatically where a retry could email someone twice, and the delivery keeps its place so nothing else sends in its stead. If the customer confirms it never arrived, send it again by hand from the invoice.

reason_codes.meaning: Finero failed, and the cause is not something in your workspace.
reason_codes.resolution: Report it to Finero support with the execution's timestamp.

x-permissions.description: Each operation declares the LEAST key permission that may call it in `x-permission`. An `admin` key satisfies every operation; a `readonly` key satisfies only operations whose `x-permission` is `readonly`. The router enforces this from the same classification this document is generated from — the check is never inferred from the HTTP method. These are key PERMISSIONS, not OAuth scopes: this scheme is HTTP bearer, and OpenAPI declares `scopes` only on `oauth2`/`openIdConnect` schemes. Finero's OAuth surface is the MCP server, which publishes RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at `https://app.getfinero.com/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. Access there is granted on a consent screen, where a person lets the agent act as them, and every call is checked against that person's own permissions — not by OAuth scope values; the authorization server accepts only `openid`.
